commits.message:
effects-feel: each loop's measured line asserted by name, the wait bounded by the test's own budget (rich-unfiled-791c.2iki)

Review (high): counting 'worst contrast' matches >= 5 counted frames, not
loops; at 1 fps a machine that measures every loop between two ticks
paints the four lines once and fails. The 30_000 wait copied HANG_MS.

effects-feel measures every loop's contrast at 1 fps, not 30 (rich-unfiled-791c.2iki)

The demo paints on a wall-clock rate, so its frames cost the same each
second however loaded the machine is, and the contrast measuring gets
what is left. At 30 fps under a full suite that was little: 7.4-10.6 s
locally, 21 s of 30 on CI. At 1 fps, 4.1-5.2 s under the full suite
(three runs), 2.0 s alone (was 2.8 s).

The theme grid's notice reads whole, and the row test searches only rows that can be cut (rich-demos-k78j.4jr)

Each notice line now sits in the notice column instead of the two lines
being cropped as one; at 100 columns every theme had lost 'see incident'.
The test missed it because a phrase counted as shown when it appeared in any
panel body. It now compares unwrapped rows to unwrapped rows, fails when the
roomy run paints nothing, pages by the header's section count, reads titles
from any box corner, and drives the dropdown status row to its widest.

Two demos' rows read whole in their card's terminal (rich-demos-k78j.4jr)

rich-template-bindings: every editor-panel title now fits the 34 cells a
half-row panel gives it in an 80-column terminal (44 at the card's 100), and
the nav hint fits 80 columns instead of losing "Ctrl+C: exit". At the card
size five titles were cut, not the three the checkpoint counted.

dropdown-demo: the pointer readout moves to its own row; beside the three
dropdowns' state it ran the status to 114 cells.

test/examples/demo-rows.test.ts runs each demo in a roomy headless xterm and
in its card's, and fails on any title, rule or unboxed row the roomy screens
show that the card's do not show whole. It fails on the pre-fix demos with
every cut above.

A Spinner draws the frame for the time it is handed (rich-animation-xi28.6k9)

Spinner read Date.now() in its constructor and on every draw, so a Progress
on a hand-moved Clock turned its spinners on real time, against
core/clock.ts's rule that nothing rendered reads a clock. It is now Frames
over the named spinner data, drawn at a `t` its host hands in, scaled by
`speed`, as Rich's Spinner.render(time) is handed console.get_time() or
task.get_time(). SpinnerColumn builds one at task.time; Live takes a
renderable or a `(t) => Renderable` view and reads its clock once a frame
to hand `t` in, as App does; Status is that view over its message and takes
a `clock`, so a test can drive it.
A transition settles its last cell as it is done, on any element (rich-unfiled-791c.7b9h) (#408)
